name: Male infertility due to gonadal dysgenesis or sperm disorder
aliases: Male infertility secondary to gonadal dysgenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and laboratory criteria for male infertility due to gonadal dysgenesis or sperm disorder

criteria.description: Histological or imaging evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or underdeveloped testes
Abnormal semen parameters including azoospermia, oligospermia, or severe sperm morphological abnormalities
Elevated gonadotropins (FSH, LH) with low or normal testosterone levels indicating primary testicular failure
Identification of chromosomal abnormalities or gene mutations associated with gonadal dysgenesis or spermatogenic failure
Presence of small, firm testes and absence of secondary sexual characteristics in severe cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of gonadal dysgenesis or abnormal semen analysis plus hormonal dysregulation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and clinical features support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Complete absence of sperm in ejaculate
Small, underdeveloped testes on physical exam or imaging

common.notes: Decreased sexual desire in some patients
Defective sperm production confirmed by biopsy or semen analysis

occasional.notes: Breast tissue enlargement due to hormonal imbalance
Decreased facial/body hair and muscle mass
searchTerms: lack of typical male puberty signs

occasional.notes: Anxiety or depression secondary to infertility diagnosis
searchTerms: psychological issues related to inability to conceive

rare.notes: Undescended testes present in some cases
Abnormally small penis in severe gonadal dysgenesis
Chromosomal anomalies detected in minority of cases

laboratory: Elevated serum FSH and LH levels
imaging: Testicular ultrasound showing hypoplastic or dysgenetic testes
genetic: Mutations in genes related to testicular development or spermatogenesis (e.g., SRY, NR5A1)
other: Testicular biopsy demonstrating impaired spermatogenesis or gonadal dysgenesis

distinguishingFeatures: Normal testicular size in early stages

redFlags: Complete azoospermia with small, firm testes
Elevated gonadotropins indicating primary testicular failure
references: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Diagnostic evaluation of the infertile male: a committee opinion. Fertil Steril. 2015.
